A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, prompts, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and revised material.

before.justification: V2 reports original model evaluations on mathematical benchmarks and four puzzle environments, including accuracy, token use, algorithm-provision ablations, and reasoning-trace analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds QwQ/Qwen comparisons and algorithm-provision results for non-reasoning DeepSeek-V3.

M1.justification: The puzzle-based evaluation framework, move extraction, simulator verification, and supplied algorithm scratchpads remain unchanged. Additional model evaluations do not introduce a new solver, architecture, or training method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MATH-500, AIME24, AIME25, Tower of Hanoi, Checker Jumping, River Crossing, and Blocks World. V3's expanded Blocks World motivation describes the alternating-stack configurations already documented in v2.

E2.justification: V3 adds the QwQ-32B/Qwen2.5-32B comparison in Figure 12 and DeepSeek-V3 to the algorithm-provision comparison in Figure 17. Revised Figure 11 drops the displayed o3-mini-high panel, although Section A.4.2 still mentions it. The corrected DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B name identifies a retained model.

E3.justification: The added model comparisons reuse existing experimental conditions: Qwen explicitly follows the main setup, and DeepSeek-V3 receives the already documented algorithm-provision treatment. Existing generation limits, temperatures, response filtering, puzzle configurations, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section A.5 examines token allocation against compositional depth across puzzles. Section A.6 extends algorithm provision to a non-reasoning model to investigate an instruction-following explanation. The sampling ablation, first-failure analyses, and qualitative trace examples already appear in v2.

E5.justification: Both versions report 25 samples per model, puzzle instance, and complexity level. Existing scatter plots, averages, and failure distributions retain their reporting practices. Additional plotted Hanoi trials do not introduce new run counts, seed information, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 12 adds QwQ/Qwen accuracy and token results; for example, QwQ's River Crossing accuracy falls from about 60% at N=2 to zero at N=3. Figure 17 adds DeepSeek-V3 algorithm-provision scores. Figure 18 also displays previously unshown Hanoi trial points at N=11–12. Original main-text results are retained.

T1.justification: The compositional-depth definition and puzzle complexity formulas, including 2^N - 1 for Hanoi and (N + 1)^2 - 1 for Checker Jumping, remain unchanged. No new or revised formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The conclusion removes the extrapolation that current approaches may encounter fundamental barriers to generalizable reasoning. The central claims about three complexity regimes, accuracy collapse, declining reasoning effort, and algorithm-execution limitations remain, making this a limited narrowing of claimed implications.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the new algorithm-provision control as favoring compositional representation and planning limitations over instruction-following deficits, and discusses nonmonotonic token allocation across compositional depths. Appendix A.1 removes the blanket assertion that tool access cannot improve reasoning. Existing applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: After matching naming corrections and relocated passages, the API/local-server information, hyperparameters, prompts, simulators, regex extraction, tokenizer, and pseudocode documentation are unchanged. The new Qwen comparison refers back to the existing setup; no new code or data access information is provided.

R1.justification: V3 adds Zhao et al. on planning with action-sequence similarity, reference 49, to contextualize Blocks World, and Li et al. on reasoning-related instruction-following failures, reference 50, to motivate the new control. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized edits to the introduction, related work, conclusion, and criticism responses, including numbering and wording corrections. It adds Section A.5 and reorganizes extended analyses under A.6, while preserving the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figures 12 and 17, changes Figure 11 from three accuracy panels to two accuracy and two token-use panels, and redraws the Hanoi row in the renumbered Figure 18. Other appendix figures and examples move, while the main figures retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The additional QwQ/Qwen comparison and non-reasoning algorithm control modestly strengthen the empirical support, while removal of sweeping extrapolations improves restraint. These gains remain limited: the new control does not establish the proposed failure mechanism, and Section A.4.2 still describes an o3-mini panel absent from revised Figure 11. Overall, the benefits support a modest net improvement.
